title: Iowa: state OSHA plan, rules not yet read
topic: State safety plan: who enforces and what differs
text: Iowa runs its own OSHA-approved plan (Iowa OSHA) covering private employers and state and local government, according to OSHA's list of State Plans. A plan must be at least as effective as federal OSHA, so the federal rules are the floor on a job there: trench protection from 5 ft or shallower when a competent person sees a cave-in hazard (29 CFR 1926.652), a ladder from 4 ft within 25 ft, the construction confined space rule (29 CFR 1926 Subpart AA), fall protection at 6 ft, and reporting a death within 8 hours and a hospitalization, amputation or eye loss within 24 hours (29 CFR 1904.39). This state's own rules were not read for this library: it is not confirmed whether the plan is stricter on trenching, confined space, heat, fall protection, training or reporting times. Ask Iowa OSHA before relying on the federal number, and report serious injuries to the state agency.

title: Indiana: IOSHA adopts the federal rules; a state excavation standard is listed
topic: State safety plan: who enforces and what differs
text: Indiana's plan, IOSHA, "adopts all OSHA standards and regulations", per OSHA's page for the plan, and OSHA's directory of state standards lists the state among those that adopt federal standards identically. The same page says the state has "a unique excavations standard." That standard could not be found or read on 2026-11-20: IOSHA's trenching page points only to federal OSHA materials, so what the state excavation standard adds is not confirmed. Until it is read, the federal rule is the floor: a protective system from 5 ft (29 CFR 1926.652), a ladder from 4 ft within 25 ft, spoil 2 ft back, daily inspections by a competent person. Reporting follows 29 CFR 1904.39 (8 hours for a death, 24 hours for a hospitalization, amputation or eye loss) if the adoption is identical. Ask IOSHA about the state excavation standard before bidding trench work there.
source: OSHA Indiana State Plan page; OSHA state standards directory
note: HELD: Indiana excavation standard not found

title: Michigan confined space rule for construction (MIOSHA Part 35)
text: Michigan's construction confined space standard is MIOSHA Construction Safety and Health Standard Part 35 (R 408.43501 to R 408.43510), titled as adopted and referenced standards. OSHA's adoption table for the 2015 federal construction rule lists this state as identical, which would make the permit items the 16 in 29 CFR 1926.1206. But OSHA's current page for the state's plan lists "Confined Spaces" among the construction subjects where MIOSHA requirements differ from federal. The Part 35 rule text could not be opened on 2026-11-19 or 2026-11-20 (only its table of contents), so whether anything differs is not confirmed. Until it is read, follow the federal construction rule as the floor and ask MIOSHA about any added state requirement.
source: MIOSHA Construction Part 35, R 408.43501-43510; OSHA Michigan State Plan page; OSHA adoption table 2015-05-04

title: California written Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP)
topic: State safety plan: written programs and training
text: California requires every employer to have a written Injury and Illness Prevention Program; OSHA's page for the state's plan lists the "Injury and Illness Prevention Program" as one of the standards unique to Cal/OSHA, along with heat exposure. For construction the rule is 8 CCR 1509, which works with the general rule 8 CCR 3203; the heat plan may be part of the IIPP (8 CCR 3395(i)). The text of 1509 and 3203 was not read on 2026-11-20, so the required contents (a responsible person, hazard inspections, training, a code of safe practices, tailgate meetings and how often) are not confirmed here: read 8 CCR 1509 before quoting an interval. Federal OSHA has no matching written-program rule for construction; its general duty is 29 CFR 1926.20(b).
source: OSHA California State Plan page; 8 CCR 1509; 8 CCR 3203; 8 CCR 3395(i)

title: Washington fall protection: one chapter, 4 feet and a work plan at 10 feet
text: Washington puts fall protection for all industries in chapter 296-880 WAC, Unified Safety Standards for Fall Protection. Its section titles show the structure: fall protection required regardless of height (296-880-10010), fall protection required at four feet or more (296-880-200 and 296-880-20005), a fall protection work plan required at ten feet or more (296-880-10020), and specific rules for construction work (296-880-30005). Only the chapter's table of contents was read on 2026-11-20, so the heights for particular construction tasks, and how the rule treats the edge of a trench, are not confirmed here: read WAC 296-880-30005 before relying on a number. For crossings the excavation rule is clear: guardrails where walkways are four feet or more above lower levels (WAC 296-155-655(12)). Federal OSHA's general construction trigger is 6 feet (29 CFR 1926.501(b)(1)).
edition: Chapter 296-880 WAC table of contents, read 2026-11-20
